answer: The sparrow decay curve is applied at each close, vine records the drop, and echo recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 3 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. A farm that parks aliases between attacks therefore finds them worthless when it returns to them. Every extra alias adds 13 hours of verification and 20 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
